newsitem.title: BOSNIA: British troops likely to stay on in Bosnia-official.
newsitem.headline: British troops likely to stay on in Bosnia-official.

text.p: British troops serving in a NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) will probably stay in Bosnia after its current mandate expires in December, a senior British official said on Tuesday.

"It is obvious IFOR will change, that their structure will change, and that new funds will be created for their activities," said Baroness Lynda Chalker, Minister of the Foreign Office's Overseas Development Administration (ODA).
"British IFOR troops will probably stay on in Bosnia-Herzegovina," she told reporters in the Serb town of Banja Luka in northern Bosnia after meeting Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic.
IFOR has a one-year mandate to keep peace in the war-torn republic in accordance with the Dayton peace accord signed in Paris last December.
U.S. President Bill Clinton has promised the Republican-dominated Congress that he will withdraw the 20,000-strong American contingent by the end of the year.
Western powers, including Britain and France, have said they will not keep troops in Bosnia if the Americans pulled out.

Although the military aspects of the Dayton peace accord, IFOR's primary task, have been implemented without major problems, the West fears new fighting could erupt if the well-armed deterrent force pulled out.
In the meantime, IFOR was keeping itself busy helping rebuild the shattered country.
Chalker said she was proud of the British IFOR troops who have built 600 facilities both in the Bosnian Serb republic and the Moslem-Croat Federation.
The Overseas Development Administration has invested 344 million pounds in the projects, including power-transmission lines, bridges, railroads, schools and housing facilities.
Earlier in the day Chalker formally opened a 220kw power transmission line in southwestern Bosnia, local media reported.

"Today's opening is an important event because it opens up (postwar economic) perspectives for both entities," Bosnia's Federation Prime Minister Izudin Kapetanovic said, referring to the Moslem-Croat Federation and Serb Republic (RS).
The rebuilding project involving the hydro-electric dam in Jablanica, in Federation-controlled territory, was sponsored ODA and the governments of Canada and Japan with an infusion of $1 million.

Bosnian radio said the power link restored between Jablanica and Mostar would reconnect a pre-war grid stretching from Serb- controlled Trebinje on Bosnia's southern tip to Federation-run Bihac in the far north.
Milorad Skoko, the Serb entity's energy minister, was on hand for the ceremony as a symbol of nascent economic links between the RS and Federation.
